title: This Way Gone

beats.what: Kenny moves his father Khatri Sr. into Colony House for his own safety after the older man tried to open the door the previous night
Boyd learns Sara has returned through the Faraway Tree and hides her in the church basement
Boyd confesses Sara's history to Kenny: she heard voices, opened a door, killed people including Khatri Sr.
Boyd has a tremor episode in Kristi's clinic; Kristi examines him and notices something under the skin of his arm
Jim tells Tabitha he heard a voice on the radio just before the house collapsed; the voice knew his name and warned about the digging
Boyd hallucinates a conversation with his dead wife, who challenges him over what telling Kenny the truth would actually accomplish
Kenny finds out the truth about his father from Sara's presence; confronts Boyd and ends the partnership

character_beats.beat: Wants to protect Sara because she was useful in the forest and may still be the key home; tells Kenny a partial truth while concealing the rest, and the hallucination of his dead wife names this for what it is: guilt management dressed as strategy
Wants to trust Boyd as the father figure who replaced his own; the episode strips that away when he pieces together that Boyd knew Sara killed Khatri Sr. and said nothing

Wants to share the radio-voice discovery and get Donna's help investigating; Donna shuts him down immediately, saying those watching them are not helping and the bus-radio incident already cost people

key_lines.line: She killed her own brother! She tried to kill a nine-year-old kid!
key_lines.why: Kenny's first moment of reckoning with the full list of what Sara did; establishes the weight Boyd is asking him to set aside

key_lines.line: You know what you have to do.
key_lines.why: Sara tells Boyd the only logical outcome of her return; he refuses to hear it, which is the contradiction

key_lines.line: Leaders sometimes have to make tough decisions, Boyd.
key_lines.why: The hallucinated dead-wife voice argues for keeping the secret from Kenny; reveals what Boyd is telling himself

key_lines.line: You watch your own fucking six.
key_lines.why: Kenny's exit line to Boyd after the confrontation; the deputy bond is severed

open_loops: The voice on the radio knew Jim's name and warned about the digging; who or what was on the other end and why warn instead of help?
Kristi noticed something moving under the skin of Boyd's arm after the forest trip: what did Martin's blood do to him?
Sara says a little boy in white told her the tree would be safe and that she and Boyd made the place angry: what does making the place angry mean mechanically?
Boyd's hallucination of his dead wife has detailed knowledge of his choices and frames them in strategic terms: is this grief, or something the place is doing to his mind?
The bus driver took the route that day as an accidental last shift; the episode asks whether that is coincidence: how do people get drawn to the place?

payoffs.what: Boyd finally states to Kenny in full what Sara did to Khatri Sr.: the long-concealed origin of Boyd's guilt is spoken aloud
The radio voice that warned Jim during the storm in S02E01 is revisited and Jim names it to Tabitha as proof someone outside can see them

contradiction.wants: to keep Kenny's trust and maintain Sara as a resource for finding a way home
contradiction.does: withholds the truth about Sara killing Khatri Sr. while confessing just enough to seem honest, and the hallucinatory voice he consults names the real motive as guilt relief, not community welfare

tone_notes: Runtime 46.9 min, 785 cues, 92.8 words/min. Two major silences: 326-455s (129 seconds, the longest single gap across this block, covering Boyd hiding Sara and then deciding to tell Kenny) and 1339-1413s (74 seconds around Boyd trying to be alone and the bus driver's confession). Density spikes at minutes 32-33 (146-156, the Boyd-Kenny confrontation) and 13-14 (131-136, the Sara reveal argument). Boyd's name is mentioned 21 times and Kenny's 18 times, more than any other character, centring the episode firmly on their relationship. 'Need to talk' appears five times, flagging the episode as one driven by deferred conversation.
